subject: botany
question_text: Who discovered the cell and what was the book written by him?

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book's printed answer is partly hidden by scan noise but clearly reads Robert Hooke / Micrographia; the cork detail added here is the standard NCERT account.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Discoverer of the cell
lines: Robert Hooke discovered the cell. He saw
small box-like compartments in a thin slice
of cork under his microscope and named
steps.why: The first half asks for the discoverer; the one-line cork observation shows how the discovery happened and makes the name stick.
common_mistakes: Writing Leeuwenhoek — he observed living cells later; Hooke saw the first (dead cork) cells.
Writing Robert Brown — he discovered the nucleus, not the cell.
steps.memory_tip: Cellula means a small room; Hooke saw cork divided into small rooms and named them cells.
steps.margin_note: Name plus one line on the cork observation.

steps.label: His book
lines: He described and drew his microscope
steps.why: The second half asks for the book. Micrographia, where Hooke published his microscope drawings, completes the answer.
common_mistakes: Misspelling the title — it is Micrographia, one word.
Writing De Historia Plantarum — that is Theophrastus' book.
steps.memory_tip: Micro-graphia = small drawings — a book of what the microscope showed.
steps.margin_note: The boxed name-and-book line carries this mark.

insider_note: Discovery questions pair a person with a book; answer in that fixed pattern — name first, title second — and both marks are earned.
